column1: # recipe corrections of retained-port-20261107 (m3/llm), one row per correction made while producing this leaf

column2: --seal computed the m3/pom.xml postimage from the checkout (already registered) and wrote <module>llm</module> twice
column3: the reactor preimage is always the base blob eadf233183d4 read with git cat-file, never the checkout; the anchor must occur exactly once in that blob

column2: jdk_naming.py plan --only m3/llm/ reported PKG_COM_M3/PKG_PATH_COM_M3 rewrites inside apply.py (its donor prefixes and docstring) and would have broken the recipe
column3: donor package spans and the legacy SYNEXIA- prefix are spelled in two concatenated parts in apply.py; prose says "the com.m3.* namespace"; the plan reports 0 rewrites on the recipe

column2: after the package relocation the naming plan still reported CONST_KEBAB=1 in ChromeMlTaskService (schema id SYNEXIA-CHROMEML-CAPABILITIES/1)
column3: folded as the one EDITS entry (ADAPT, //FLLDCIM: MRL anchor) so apply.py alone produces the jdk_naming fixed point; declared in the differential (one line) and covered by mutant M1

column2: the written module tree disappeared from the worktree once (reflog: reset: moving to HEAD) before the first commit; a stray 1-byte NOTICE appeared
column3: commit right after apply.py and after every gate; never git checkout HEAD -- <path> in the shared-clone worktree (git show HEAD:<path> > <path> instead); apply.py refuses a drifted target so a partial tree is detected, not overwritten

column2: PATH="$JAVA_HOME/bin:$PATH" with a Windows JAVA_HOME was not honoured by Git Bash; javac 17 compiled the donor and failed on List.getFirst()
column3: every JDK tool in the gate scripts is called by absolute path under the JDK 21 home

column2: javap prints CRLF on Windows; piping one side through sed made every line differ
column3: tr -d '\r' on both sides before the diff (javap_parity.sh)

column2: passing -Djava.io.tmpdir both as a user property and in argLine makes surefire warn "configured twice"
column3: the forked JVM gets it through argLine, the Maven JVM through MAVEN_OPTS; no bare user property
